intent: Dates that mean something: typed entries, lead days, and the one module both arms consume.
change: Calendar entry semantics in packages/engine: deadline and subscription_renewal types, per-entry reminder lead days, auto-cancel flag and lead threshold, due-computation over entries, send/enqueue idempotence keys, and the entry annotation states (handled, declined, needs-attention, late).
done_when: Unit tests prove due computation across types, lead days, and boundary dates; integration tests prove annotation transitions persist on the s1 schema and idempotence keys are unique per (entry, day) and (entry, renewal).

proofs.claim: Before the calendar ledger exists, the suite that marks an entry, records one reminder per (entry, day) and one auto-cancel per (entry, renewal) on the migrated schema cannot load: it fails at import because the db calendar-ledger module is not there.

On the s1 schema plus migration 0007, an entry carries its lead days, auto-cancel flag and threshold with defaults; a mark on an entry persists with note and time and only a mark of equal or higher rank may replace it; recordReminder is one row per (entry, day) and recordAutoCancel one per (entry, renewal), returning the existing row on a repeat, with the database itself refusing a duplicate; the records go with the entry; and the migration set still creates exactly the declared tables and re-applies as a no-op.

Due computation is right across both kinds, lead days, and boundary dates: a reminder is owed from the lead day to the date and late after the first day, an auto-cancel from its own threshold to the renewal and never for a deadline, a done, handled, undated or unflagged entry; date arithmetic crosses months, years and leap days on the string and reads the day off the person’s clock; annotation ranks refuse a weaker mark over a stronger one; the dispatch vocabularies and keys are what the scan will write; the schema declares the new tables, cascades and unique keys and the package exports them.
Lint, typecheck (build and test configs), the full suite with coverage thresholds (100% on core), and both builds pass with the calendar semantics in place.

intent: The daily heartbeat: every dated entry becomes exactly one timely Telegram nudge.
change: pg-boss cron scan job computing due reminders and dispatching through s3's sendToUser with record-before-dispatch idempotence, delivered/failed/skipped-unbound/late states, bounded retry on next scan, and late-send for missed windows.
done_when: Integration tests with a scripted send sink prove exactly-once under re-run and crash-between-record-and-dispatch, unbound-user skip, failed-send retry on next scan, late-marked sends after a downtime window, and pickup of chat-created entries.

intent: The renewal date that pulls a trigger - but only a human can release the safety.
change: The scan's auto-cancel arm enqueuing an s5 cancellation task once per renewal date, the leading Telegram confirm question via the UserIO gate, promotion of s3 pending-question routing to the production UserIO implementation (scripted double retained for tests), and entry annotation on every ending.
done_when: Integration tests on fixtures via LocalProvider with scripted UserIO prove confirm-yes through to a cancelled fixture member with event trail, decline and timeout leaving membership untouched and the entry annotated, unlinked-entry needs-attention with the reminder still sent, and enqueue idempotence under re-run.

intent: The proof no fixture can fake: a real phone buzzes, a real yes, the task finishes.
change: The live proof workflow gated on TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN: a real reminder delivered to the bound account, and the full auto-cancel round-trip - real confirm question in Telegram, real answer, task resumes and completes against the fixture - with skip-with-reason when the token is absent and the run recorded.
done_when: The gated live suite delivers a real reminder and completes the confirm round-trip against the fixture with the task succeeded and events recorded; without the token the suite skips with an explicit reason; the run procedure is documented in the repo.
